To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

perceived organizational support is positively related to employees' motivation to use new IT, and that this relationship is mediated by the intrinsic and identified motivation, but not the extrinsic motivation, to use the IT.
(1) perceived organizational support and (2) distributive justice are positively related to (3) intrinsic motivation to use the new IT.

(1) Perceived organizational support and distribative justice affect employees' motivation to use new IT; (2) Intrinsic and extrinsically motivated employees use new IT to the same extent, but only those who are intrinsically motivated accept and enjoy the IT and use it to the same extent as those who use a paper-based alternative; and (3) Employees' intrinsic motivation to use IT mediates the effects of perceived organizational support on enjoyment and acceptance of new IT.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the role of perceived organizational and distributive justice in employees’ reactions to new information technologies (IT) and the motivational processes through which these relationships operate.
understanding how employees react to organizational interventions, in this case new IT.
how employees react to organizational changes, in particular the implementation of new information technology

perceived organizational support is a strong predictor of intrinsic motivation and that intrinsic motivation is a strong predictor for IT usage.
the results of this study suggest that perceived organizational support is a key factor in the success of IT implementations.

employees' reactions to new IT are affected by their perceptions of the organization's level of support, and by their perceptions of distributive justice, and that the relationship between POS and distributive justice and employee reactions is mediated by intrinsic motivation.
perceived organizational support (POS) and distributive justice are important antecedents of intrinsic and identified motivation.

employees who perceive that their organization is supportive, and who believe that the organization treats them fairly in the implementation of new IT, will experience more positive reactions to the IT.

perceived organizational support is important in IT implementations.
